updates.name: Dieffenbachia (dumb cane), lime/cream form
updates.note: Added environment details: light (PAR, DLI), VPD, soil, nutrients and pests

water_notes: Water when the top 1-2 in (3-5 cm) of mix is dry. Soak until water drains out, then empty the saucer. Indoors in winter this stretches to every 10-14 days. Cold, wet mix is the commonest way to lose these plants.
soil_medium: Chunky, fast-draining aroid mix: about 40% potting soil, 30% orchid bark, 20% perlite or pumice and 10% coco coir or worm castings. The pot must have drainage holes.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid, such as 3-1-2 or 20-20-20, at half strength
nutrients: Feed every 2-4 weeks from March to September at half strength, and stop from November to February. Pale new leaves point to low nitrogen. Yellow older leaves with green veins point to low magnesium (1 tsp Epsom salt per gallon, once a season). Brown crisp tips can be salt build-up: flush the pot with plain water every 2-3 months.
pests_watch:
Spider mites: fine webbing and stippled leaves, worst in dry heated air
Thrips: silvery streaks and black specks on leaves
Mealybugs: white cottony clumps in leaf joints
Fungus gnats: small flies over damp mix
Root rot from cold, soggy mix
Bacterial or fungal leaf spot: brown, water-soaked spots
pest_steps:
Check leaf undersides and leaf joints once a week, and before any plant comes indoors.
Keep newly moved plants apart from the others for 2 weeks.
Wipe leaves with a damp cloth to remove dust and mites.
For mites, thrips or mealybugs: spray insecticidal soap or neem oil every 5-7 days for three rounds. Test one leaf first and do not spray in hot sun.
For mealybugs on a few spots: touch each with a swab of 70% rubbing alcohol.
For fungus gnats: let the top inch of mix dry, add yellow sticky traps, and water once with Bti (Mosquito Bits) soaked water.
Remove leaves with leaf spot, keep the foliage dry and give the plant airflow.
pests_current: No pests identified in the photos so far. Note here anything you see, with the date.

updates.name: Boobie cactus (Fukurokuryuzinboku)
updates.note: Added environment details: light (PAR, DLI), VPD, soil, nutrients and pests

water_notes: Soak the pot, then let it dry completely before watering again: about every 2-3 weeks in summer, and almost none in winter (once a month at most, and never below 45 F). Wet roots plus cold is how cacti die.
soil_medium: Mostly mineral: about two parts pumice, crushed granite or coarse sand to one part potting soil. The pot must have drainage holes.
fertilizer: Low-nitrogen cactus fertilizer, about 2-7-7, at half strength
nutrients: Feed once a month from April to August. None in autumn and winter. Etiolation (thin, stretched growth) means too little light, not too little food.
pests_watch:
Mealybugs and scale (cochineal scale looks like white cotton on prickly pear pads)
Root and base rot
Fungal rot after frost damage
Fungus gnats

Inspect the crown and leaf bases with a flashlight every few weeks.
Treat mealybugs and scale by dabbing them with 70% rubbing alcohol on a swab; repeat weekly until gone.
Keep water out of the crown, and keep the mix dry through cold weather.
If a stem turns soft or black, cut well above it with a clean blade and let the cut dry for a week before replanting.
Quarantine any new plant for 2 weeks.

updates.name: Fig

water_notes: Water deeply when the top 2 in of mix is dry, which in summer heat can be every 2-3 days in a pot. In winter it is dormant: water about once a month, just enough that the roots do not dry out.

fertilizer: Slow-release 8-8-8 or compost

Leaf spot

Rake up and bin fallen leaves in autumn to lower rust and leaf spot.
Water at the base, not over the leaves.
Treat scale and mites with horticultural oil while the tree is dormant.
Mulch to keep the roots cool and moist.

Look under leaves and at growing tips once a week.
Knock aphids and mites off with a strong spray of water in the morning.

For mildew, remove the worst leaves, water at the base and give the plant airflow.
